audit.why: 47.56% over 757 games — a real losing lane. HARD / 7.5-difficulty framing matches: Sett is zero-resource, out-brawls Cho'Gath levels 1-5, and Cho'Gath only stabilises through scaling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers hand all seven stages to Sett. That contradicts the page's own whys[]: whys[4] says 'It's a coinflip here' (Level 6) and whys[6] says 'It tips to you once Feast is online' (2+ items). The packet chart agrees with the whys, not the win array.
audit.why: At 6 both ultimates arrive together — Feast (80/70/60s) versus The Show Stopper (120/100/80s) — so it is genuinely even, not Sett's. At two-plus items Feast stacks plus resists survive the brawl and Cho'Gath's knockup-silence peels the Show Stopper engage, which is where the 2+ item stage tips.
audit.corrected: Level 6 Skill (5/10), 2+ items Cho'Gath (6/10). Proposed as one atomic chart group across both layers; the other five stages stay Sett.

audit.whatIsWrong: The single most important interaction in this matchup is absent everywhere: Knuckle Down (Q) deals damage based on the target's MAX HEALTH. Cho'Gath's whole win condition is stacking health with Feast, and every stack he takes makes Sett's Q hit harder. Second omission: Facebreaker (E) only STUNS if enemies are on opposite sides of Sett — a lone Cho'Gath with nothing behind Sett is only slowed. The page's dontsFull entry 'Get E-stunned' carried generic filler text instead of that rule.
audit.why: Riot text — Knuckle Down: 'Sett's next two attacks deal additional damage based off of the target's max health.' Facebreaker: 'pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him, dealing damage and stunning them. If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Haymaker: Sett 'passively stores damage he takes as Grit' and cashes it as a shield plus true damage — so poking Sett literally arms his answer. Cooldowns: Q 9/8/7/6/5, W 18/16.5/15/13.5/12, E 16/14.5/13/11.5/10, R 120/100/80, all at zero resource cost.
audit.corrected: Knuckle Down's max-health damage stated in report[5].t and wants.foe[0]; the Facebreaker both-sides stun rule stated in dontsFull[2].d; Grit's feed-loop stated in dosFull[0].d and breakdown.cooldowns with real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Haymaker but gave no cooldown number and never mentioned Facebreaker, the ability that actually starts his combo.
audit.why: Haymaker is 18s at rank 1 and Facebreaker 16s — both very long early, and Sett pays no mana, so the only thing gating him is those timers.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with both numbers and the both-sides stun condition.

audit.why: Plated Steelcaps and early Thornmail component are right against a physical-damage brawler with missing-health regen on his passive.
'Feed his grit bar' is the correct headline mistake and is not split by elo.

edits.before: Feast stacks turn you into terrain — every R is permanent HP plus a true-damage execute. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Sett's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Both ults land at once: Feast is an 80s true-damage execute, The Show Stopper a 120s suppress-and-slam. Whoever spends first loses, so bait his step-up.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Sett carry threat 7/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on: Feast stacks plus resists outlast his brawl, and your knockup into silence peels Show Stopper off your carries.

edits.before: Shield + true damage. Silence before it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Haymaker banks your poke as Grit, then returns it — silence the cast, don't feed it.

edits.before: Whiffing Q and fighting anyway — without the knockup your kit is a slow zone with no teeth.
edits.after: Facebreaker only stuns if enemies are on both sides of him — alone, off the wave, it is a slow.

edits.before: Track Sett's Haymaker: Shield + true damage. Silence before it. When it is down — Q-W + R him.
edits.after: Knuckle Down hits max health, so Feast stacks feed it. Silence Haymaker (18s) before he cashes Grit.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — Shield + true damage. Silence before it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Sett Haymaker (18s at rank 1): matchup-defining — shield plus true damage, sized by the Grit your poke gave him. - Facebreaker is 16s and only stuns from both sides. - Feast: kill windows only.

edits.before: Walk you down at levels 2-3 with Pit Grit heavy punches while you have only one ability and no waveclear
edits.after: Walk you down at 2-3 with Knuckle Down, whose max-health damage grows with every point of HP Feast gives you

notes: Packet flagged 'Show Stopper' in spikes[1].text as a probable wrong name — FALSE POSITIVE, it is a legitimate short form of The Show Stopper and reads correctly in context. Left alone. Not corrected but worth the user's eye: the page never says that Cho'Gath poking Sett is what powers Haymaker's shield size, which is the reason 'don't feed grit' is advice rather than a slogan — I put the mechanism into dosFull[0].d, but the early/mid prose still frames Grit vaguely and could carry more if the length band is ever relaxed.
